result:
The automatic `--help` option now stores its value under `_click_default_help`, so user parameters named `help` work. The full suite passes: 2260 passed, 24 skipped, 1 xfailed.

**Blocked on me:** nothing.

**Changed** (nothing committed; all changes are in the working tree):
- **`src/click/core.py`:**
  - Added the private module constant `_HELP_OPTION_STORAGE_NAME = "_click_default_help"`.
  - `get_help_option` now passes that constant as an explicit name when it builds the automatic help option. Because the help option no longer stores anything under `help`, `click.Argument(["help"])` and `click.Option(["--assist", "help"])` get their values. The explicit name also means names that aren't valid Python identifiers, like `["/?"]`, no longer produce the deprecation warning they used to trigger. The docstring mentions the reserved name and has a `versionchanged:: 8.6.0` note.
  - `get_params` has two new `UserWarning` checks:
    - An `Argument` whose storage name is also used by any other parameter: "`'<name>' is used by an argument` … they will overwrite each other's value during parsing".
    - Any parameter other than the help option itself that uses the reserved name: "reserved for the automatic help option".
  - Options that share a name with each other, like the `--upper`/`--lower` feature switches, don't warn.
- **`tests/test_info_dict.py`:** the expected help option entry now has the name `_click_default_help`.
- **`tests/test_commands.py`:** 8 new tests (9 cases):
  - the reserved name on `get_help_option` and in `to_info_dict()`
  - an argument named `help`, and the help flag still printing the help text
  - an option named `help`
  - custom help names `--man` and `/?`, with no warnings
  - each of the two new warnings
  - feature switches not warning
  - `@click.option("--help", default="default value")`: `get_help_option` returns `None`, the option gets its default or the passed value, and no help text is printed. This already worked before the change, so this test documents existing behaviour.

**Verified:**
- I temporarily undid the one-line change in `get_help_option`, and 5 of the new tests failed. I then put it back.
- `tests/test_commands.py` and `tests/test_info_dict.py`: 150 passed.
- The full suite passes, with warnings treated as errors, so no existing test triggers the new warnings.
- Lint, format check and type check (`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy`) are all clean.

**Found:**
- One side effect: if `help_option_names` contains a bare identifier like `["help"]`, building the help option now raises `TypeError: Name ... defined twice`. Before, it quietly made a help option with no flags, which couldn't be used anyway. I left it as is; if you'd rather it be ignored than raise, that entry would need to be filtered out.
- The new warnings fire every time `get_params` runs, the same way the existing duplicate-option warning does. Python's default warning filter only shows each one once per location.
